chunks: From his proofs (peace be upon him): On the Day of Resurrection, when people are gathered barefoot, naked, and dew-clawed, Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, says to whoever worshipped this world: 'This is your world, so take it,' and He says to whoever worshipped the Hereafter: 'This is your Hereafter, so take it.'

key_terms.غُرُلًا: devoid of the foreskin (a sign of ease in Paradise or specific state)

ai.seo_question: How does Allah distinguish between those who worshipped the world and those who worshipped the Hereafter on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this scene to illustrate the principle of *Jaza' min jins al-'amal* (recompense in kind), where the dominant love of the heart determines one's eternal state. This reflects the Shia theological emphasis on how worldly attachment (*hubb al-dunya*) or Hereafter-oriented devotion (*hubb al-akhirah*) shapes the soul's ultimate destination, serving as a practical guide for self-assessment (*muhasaba*).
